projects.title: Creative Systems
projects.summary: Layered interface studies with responsive motion and fluid input.
detail: This project studies how an interface can feel physical without becoming heavy. The visual system uses dark surfaces, repeated media layers, subtle cursor response, and staged transitions.
The page is designed as a compact motion case study: thumbnail first, short context second, then a deeper detail view with related images and an external reference link.

projects.title: Layered Interfaces
projects.summary: Hover states, depth shifts, and link moments for a dark portfolio index.
detail: A focused interaction set built around layered image response. Each state keeps the base layout readable while letting media react to pointer position, page changes, and link intent.
The transition behavior is inspired by repeating image motion: old thumbnails echo outward while the next page enters in staggered layers.

projects.title: Local Preview
projects.summary: A practical local preview and GitHub Pages publishing flow.
detail: This project documents a lightweight workflow for reviewing a static portfolio locally before release.
The goal is to keep deployment simple: preview the same static files, verify links and assets, then publish without server-only features.

projects.title: Visual Studies
projects.summary: Dark UI compositions for grid rhythm, contrast, and motion tone.
detail: A set of compact visual directions for image-led portfolio sections.
The studies focus on square crop discipline, readable overlays, and short written notes that support browsing without interrupting it.

projects.title: Micro Media
projects.summary: Compact image and motion assets designed for quick static loading.
detail: A media handling study for small portfolio pages.
The project keeps motion rich while keeping file sizes low enough for fast static delivery.

projects.title: Motion Index
projects.summary: A paged visual index where each tile behaves like a moving layer.
detail: A navigation pattern for many small works.
The index uses thumbnails first, then short context, then deeper project detail so the browsing rhythm stays fast.
